A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same concept-vector and representational-interference study on Qwen, InternVL, and Gemma. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the reorganized sections, equations, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original steering experiments, representational analyses, visual-search results, and color-similarity evaluations, including Tables 1–5 and appendix figures.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds natural-image shape steering, probe train/test evaluations, and mean-aggregation probe experiments in its appendices.

M1.justification: Appendix C.3 introduces a mean-aggregation probe variant, replacing learned attention pooling with averaged token embeddings, and also evaluates its PCA-regularized form. The original attention probes, centroid extraction, and activation-steering transformation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a 297-example VQA/COCO subset for steering shape answers on natural images, extending the previous natural-image color-steering coverage. The original synthetic conjunction, visual-search, and color-similarity tasks remain.

E2.justification: Table 12 adds Mean Agg Probe and PCA Mean Agg Probe to the compositional-steering comparison against the retained attention-probe, PCA-probe, and centroid methods. The comparator sets in the original Tables 1–5 are unchanged.

E3.justification: The new shape experiment evaluates five alternative shapes on initially correct subsets of 183, 177, and 111 examples for Qwen, InternVL, and Gemma. The synthetic-data appendix also replaces the earlier distractor range [4,40] with {2,4,8,16,24,32,40}; this revises the documented setting without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic validation through probe train/test results and attention-versus-mean pooling comparisons with and without PCA (Tables 6–7 and 10–12; Figures 9–10). Appendix B.3 and Table 9 additionally investigate natural-shape transfer failures and sensitivity to source and target shape identity.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, significance tests, or a defined uncertainty-estimation procedure. Error bars already appear in v1 Figure 6; v2 extends the same graphical reporting to additional models without introducing a new statistical practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical values, but substantial results are added in Tables 6–12. These include near-perfect attention-probe train/test accuracy, natural-shape centroid-steering success of 19.7%, 1.1%, and 25.8%, and mean-probe steering success of 53.5%, 2.9%, and 10.4% for Qwen, InternVL, and Gemma. These are newly reported outcomes, not improvements to the retained headline scores.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds the mathematical definition of the mean-aggregation predictor and its normalized concept direction in Equation 7. Existing steering, similarity, and interference definitions remain unchanged; the explicit PCA projector elaborates the previously described operation, and no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and central geometry-interference claims are retained. The introduction and conclusion narrow architectural generalizations toward the current VLM paradigm, while the conclusion adds a qualified novelty claim about observing categorical-perception-like compression in VLM latent space.

C2.justification: v2 attributes weaker natural-shape transfer to contextual ambiguity and the gap between synthetic shapes and natural object properties. It also interprets color geometry through the categorical-perception 'accordion effect', while explicitly declining to establish categorical perception itself or determine the structure's origin. The original limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C substantially improve implementation documentation with dataset sizes and sampling rules, centroid-image positions, probe training/test construction, SGD learning rate, color-probe batch size, scheduling, early stopping, and greedy decoding. These mostly disclose previously unspecified details rather than establish changed experiments. The code-access link points to the same repository.

R1.justification: v2 adds Harnad and Goldstone to develop the categorical-perception connection, Assouel and Conklin in the compression discussion, and Goyal for the added dataset. These are localized extensions of the existing positioning; the Frankland and Nurisso references are updated versions of already cited work.

P1.justification: The former Experiments section is reorganized into representation extraction and validation, representational structure, and geometry–behavior sections. The introduction gains explicit contribution statements and a roadmap, the appendices are extensively reorganized and expanded, and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: v2 substantially changes typography, spacing, and figure placement, including separating Figures 3–8 from their discussion. It adds Tables 6–12 and Figures 9–11; Table 12 redisplays the original compositional results alongside new comparators. The original extended Figures 9–10 are retained as Figures 12–13.

improvement.justification: The added data-generation and training details improve reproducibility, while probe-quality checks, pooling ablations, and shape-transfer failures make the steering evidence easier to assess. The categorical-perception qualification also improves calibration. However, the central numerical evidence and unresolved causal interpretation remain largely unchanged, and several figures are now distant from their discussion. The net improvement is useful but limited.
